body.title: Custom agent model pin is overridden by the model selected in Copilot chat or the GitHub cloud window

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in (version not captured in the original report)
- VS Code Version: current stable / insiders as of 2026-09-30 (exact build not captured)
- OS Version: not captured
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): custom agent selection in Copilot chat, and in the GitHub cloud / Cloud session window
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): whichever model is already selected in the chat or cloud window; it differs from the model pinned in the custom agent
- Logs: not attached. Chat debug view should show the request model matching the window picker, not the `.agent.md` `model` field.

## Summary

Selecting a custom agent does not honor the model pinned in that agent's frontmatter. The model already selected in the Copilot chat window, or in the GitHub cloud window, overrides the pin. The agent then runs on the window's model.

This is not the same as frontmatter failing to load. Instructions and tools can still come from the agent file. Only the pinned model loses to the window selection.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add a custom agent, for example `.github/agents/reviewer.agent.md`, with a model pin that is **not** the model currently selected in the window. Use the qualified name:

```yaml
---
name: reviewer
description: Review-only agent that must run on the pinned model
tools: [search/codebase]
model: Claude Haiku 4.5 (copilot)
---

You are a review agent. When asked which model you are using, answer with the model that actually served this request.
```

2. In the Copilot chat window, select a different model in the model picker (for example a GPT model, or Auto).
3. Select the `reviewer` custom agent from the agent dropdown.
4. Send a prompt. In the chat debug view, check the model on the request.
5. Repeat from the GitHub cloud window (Cloud session target / agents panel): leave a different model selected in that window, select the same custom agent, and start a task.

## Expected

Selecting the custom agent uses the model pinned in frontmatter (`Claude Haiku 4.5 (copilot)` in the example). The model selected in the chat or cloud window is only the fallback when `model` is omitted.

That matches the docs:

- VS Code custom agents: "`model` — The AI model to use when running the prompt. … If not specified, the currently selected model in model picker is used."
- GitHub custom agents configuration: "`model` — Model to use when this custom agent executes. If unset, inherits the default model."

A set `model` should win. The window selection should not override it.

## Actual

The model selected in the Copilot chat window, or in the GitHub cloud window, overrides the frontmatter pin. The custom agent's model selection is not honored. There is no warning that the pin was ignored.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- #321765 is a startup load bug: after restart, some agents do not load frontmatter at all (empty description, tools not applied, `user-invocable: false` agents still listed). This report is precedence, not a cache miss: the window's selected model wins over a pin that is present in the agent definition. It also happens in the GitHub cloud window, which #321765 does not cover.
- #338489 / #338629 updated guidance to say the Copilot harness supports `model` (single value and ordered list) and removed the old "unsupported" hover warning. That docs fix does not stop the window selection from overriding the pin at runtime.
- #291883 (subagent `model` not respected) was fixed in 1.109. This is the parent-session / cloud-window case.
- github/copilot-cli#2950 is the same class of bug on the CLI prompt-invocation path, not the Copilot chat or GitHub cloud window.

## Notes

- Reproduced with the qualified `Model Name (vendor)` form, not a bare API id, so this is not the unknown-model fallback in #319709 / #319131.
- An array pin (`model: [A, B]`) has the same result: the window selection is used instead of the first available entry in the list.

body.title: Test: Custom agent model preferences and required models
body.body:
Refs: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/338949, https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/345671, https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/345787

- [x] anyOS: @chrmarti regular VS Code Chat
- [ ] anyOS: @amunger Agents window, local Copilot CLI

Complexity: 3

**Time limit: 19 minutes per tester, including setup and cleanup. Pick one surface above; do not repeat the whole plan on both.**


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23345911%0A%0A&assignees=aeschli)

---

Custom agents can suggest models and reasoning effort, or require a set of models. An omitted `model-policy` behaves like `preferred`. Manual preferred-model overrides affect the conversation and last-used selection, not `chat.defaultModel`. Required agents must not silently use an unrelated model or Auto.

## Prerequisites

Use a build containing the merged #345787 and an already signed-in Copilot account with at least two available agent-capable models. A build predating that merge is insufficient. No debugger, remote host, BYOK setup, or repository build is needed for this plan. If those prerequisites are missing, report that and stop rather than spending the test budget on installation.

Report the surface, build version, and model names you used. File failures in microsoft/vscode, referencing this test-plan item.

## 1. Setup and example agents (4 minutes)

Open a disposable workspace. Note your current model and any `chat.defaultModel` setting; temporarily clear that setting to make the last-used check unambiguous.

Create these three files under `.github/agents/`. The examples use `GPT-5 (copilot)` and `Claude Sonnet 4.5 (copilot)`: **replace them with two models available in your chosen surface**, using agent-file model completion. Choose a first model that supports reasoning effort and replace `high` with a supported value if needed. Keep `tpi-nonexistent-model-12345` unchanged.

`.github/agents/tpi-preferred.agent.md`

```markdown
---
name: TPI Preferred
description: Test an agent's default model preference and reasoning effort.
model: ['GPT-5 (copilot)']
reasoning-effort: high
---
Reply only with OK. Do not use tools or modify files.
```

The missing policy is intentional: this tests the default `preferred` behavior.

`.github/agents/tpi-required.agent.md`

```markdown
---
name: TPI Required
description: Test a required set of models.
model: ['GPT-5 (copilot)', 'Claude Sonnet 4.5 (copilot)']
model-policy: required
reasoning-effort: high
---
Reply only with OK. Do not use tools or modify files.
```

`.github/agents/tpi-unavailable.agent.md`

```markdown
---
name: TPI Unavailable
description: Test blocking and recovery when a required model is unavailable.
model: ['tpi-nonexistent-model-12345']
model-policy: required
---
Reply only with OK. Do not use tools or modify files.
```

Each file must start with `---`, with exactly one frontmatter block. Confirm all three agents appear in the agent picker.

## 2. Preferred model, effort, and last-used (4 minutes)

- [ ] Start an ordinary chat with the second model selected. Select **TPI Preferred**: the picker changes to the first model and reflects the authored reasoning effort.
- [ ] Open the model picker: the authored model has an **Agent Preferred** annotation; other models remain selectable.
- [ ] Before making a manual override, start a new ordinary chat without a custom agent: it still uses the second model. Applying an agent preference must not rewrite last-used.
- [ ] Return to the preferred-agent chat and manually select the second model. Send `Reply only with OK.` The chat uses the manual choice rather than switching back to the authored model.
- [ ] Start another ordinary chat without a custom agent: it uses the manually selected second model. The manual choice is remembered as last-used, and `chat.defaultModel` has not been written.

## 3. Required models and source link (4 minutes)

- [ ] In a new chat, select **TPI Required**. The first available authored model is selected. The model picker offers only the two available authored models, annotated **Agent Required**, with no unrelated model or Auto fallback.
- [ ] The picker explains that its models are defined by **TPI Required**. Tab to the agent-source link and press Enter: the correct agent file opens in the text editor, including its frontmatter.
- [ ] Select the second allowed model and send `Reply only with OK.` It remains selected and the request succeeds. Select the first model again and change its effort: required policy restricts model identity, not effort.
- [ ] Reload the window and reopen this chat. The agent and required-model restriction survive restoration; another short request succeeds with an allowed model.

## 4. Unavailable model, draft preservation, and recovery (5 minutes)

- [ ] Select **TPI Unavailable** and type `Keep this draft while sending is blocked.` There is an explanation of the unavailable required model. Its severity border closes around the banner only, not the whole input.
- [ ] Attempt to send using Enter and the send button, if enabled. No request starts, no unrelated model or Auto is used, and the draft remains intact. The picker must not offer an unrelated workaround.
- [ ] While this agent remains selected, edit its file from `model-policy: required` to `model-policy: preferred` and save. Without reselecting the agent or reloading, the blocking explanation disappears, other models become available, and the draft remains. Select an available model and send successfully.
- [ ] Change the same file back to `required` and save. Without reselecting the agent, sending is blocked again.
- [ ] Switch to **TPI Preferred** or a built-in agent. The stale warning/restriction disappears and an ordinary request succeeds.

## 5. Cleanup and result (2 minutes)

- [ ] Restore your original `chat.defaultModel` setting and model selection; remove the three sample agent files or discard the disposable workspace.
- [ ] Comment with the surface/build/models tested and pass/fail. For a failure, include the failing checkbox, actual behavior, and a screenshot if useful. Stop at 19 minutes and identify any unchecked steps.

body.title: sessions: show the Done section by default
body.body:
fyi @benibenj 

---

<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

`sessions.list.showArchivedByDefault` now defaults to `true`: the Agents window's sessions list shows the Done section (Archived with the archive wording) unless the user hides it with the filter menu. Reset Filters now returns the section to that default instead of hiding it, and the text that said marking a session as done hides it from the list no longer says so.

Related: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9782

## Change

- The setting's `default` is now `true` instead of `false`. The rest of its registration is unchanged.
- A saved filter choice still wins over the setting. Show Done (Show Archived) in the filter menu and `showArchived` in the sessions list tool store it as `sessionsListControl.excludeArchived` in profile storage.
- Reset Filters now removes that saved choice, so the list follows `sessions.list.showArchivedByDefault` again. It used to store a choice to hide the section, which would have hidden it despite the new default. Undo still restores the previous choice.
- The Mark as Done suggestion's overview, and the matching sentence in the Agents window and chat accessibility help, now say that marking a session as done (archiving it) sets it aside instead of hiding it from the sessions list. They don't name a section, because in Inbox grouping archived sessions go to Archived while Done is a separate Inbox category. The accessibility help for marking a single nested chat as done now says that the chat keeps its own row in the Sessions list while done content is shown, and that Done only needs to be enabled in the Filter menu when it is hidden.
- `SessionsList.excludesArchivedByDefault()` still treats an unset value as hidden. The setting is registered wherever the Sessions view is, so that fallback only applies in unit tests, whose `TestConfigurationService` returns `undefined` for unset settings.
- Tests: the registration test pins `default: true`, the Reset Filters tests expect the reset to follow the setting without storing a choice, and the suggestion and accessibility help tests expect the new wording.

## How to test

1. Run this branch from sources and open the Agents window from a profile without a saved `sessionsListControl.excludeArchived`: either a fresh `--user-data-dir`, or your profile after running **Reset Filters** in the sessions filter menu, which on this branch clears the saved choice. Leave `sessions.list.showArchivedByDefault` out of your user settings.
2. Mark a session as done. It moves to the Done section at the end of the sessions list, which starts collapsed, and **Show Done** is checked in the filter menu. Before this change, the section stayed hidden until you checked Show Done.
3. Uncheck **Show Done**: the section hides, and stays hidden after a reload.
4. Run **Reset Filters**: the Done section shows again. Before this change, Reset Filters hid it. **Undo** in the notice hides it again.
5. Set `sessions.list.showArchivedByDefault` to `false` and run **Reset Filters**: the Done section is hidden.

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client` (`tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck`): passed.
- `pnpm run eslint` on the 9 changed files: passed.
- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only`: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessions.contribution.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/chatSessionArchiveNudge.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/accessibility/chatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionsChatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsListTools.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsViewMenu.test.ts`: 708 passing.
- An earlier run of the first five of those files, before the Reset Filters change, had one failure: `SessionsList inline feedback actions observes only enabled visible rows and targets one peer under multiselection (date)`. It measures a row's height after a timeout and doesn't read this setting. It passed when run alone (`--grep "observes only enabled visible rows"`: 3 passing), in a full re-run of `sessionsList.test.ts` (481 passing), and in the final run above.
- Pre-commit hygiene hook (`node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts`): passed.
- Follow-up wording commit: `pnpm run typecheck-client`, `pnpm run eslint` on its 5 files, `pnpm run build-fast --client-only`, and `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/chatSessionArchiveNudge.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/accessibility/chatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionsChatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts` (187 passing) all passed, as did the hygiene hook.
- Not run: manual testing in a running Agents window, and the component fixture screenshots. The suggestion's fixtures will render the new overview text; none of them block CI.

🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @alexdima.

body.title: Agent Host: workspace-folder change triggers catalog reconciliation that destroys an active Copilot agent-host session and deletes its session-state (data loss)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body.body:
Type: Bug Environment VS Code 1.142.0 (6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1), Windows 11 (NT 10.0.26200) Copilot agent host (copilot-runtime.exe --headless … --remote), 3 windows open Multi-root workspace with about 11 folders (main repo, several git worktrees, sibling repos) About 5 agent-host sessions open at once. Sessions had been recovered or forked earlier (.workspace-fork.lock present). What happened At 15:27:37 a workspace-folder change was processed (Claude VSCode.log: Updated lock file … with new workspace folders). All sessions logged Syncing permission mode: source=config-change. At 15:27:39, AgentHostCatalogReconciliation logged will be retried: superseded for four ahp-session:/… entries, including the actively running ahp-session:/369c23c6-a81e-4941-b412-6c4636890886. The other three were not destroyed. At 15:27:43 the host logged [Copilot:64261a3b-…] SDK session shutdown received (destroy) … lifetimeMs=3912597. The session had been running for about 65 minutes and was waiting on an elicitation. It then logged Elicitation response: cancel and Discarding elicitation callback result after abort. ~\.copilot\session-state\64261a3b-… (including events.jsonl) no longer exists. %APPDATA%\Code\agentSessionData\64261a3b-…\session.db has 0 turns, so the conversation can't be restored. At 15:32 a client action against the stale UI entry logged [AgentService] async dispatchAction failed: Session was explicitly deleted: ahp-session:/369c23c6-…. The session disappeared from the Sessions view. Nothing in the logs says who requested the delete. The same workspace-folder change and reconciliation also occurred at 14:19:51. It destroyed nothing then, because the session didn't exist yet. Expected: Reconciliation never destroys or deletes the state of a running or active session. Changing workspace folders doesn't affect existing sessions. Actual: The active session is destroyed, its on-disk state is deleted, and the UI keeps showing it until a later action fails. Steps to reproduce (inferred, not yet isolated) Open a multi-root workspace containing several folders, including git worktrees. Start several Copilot agent-host sessions. Include ones previously recovered or forked, so the catalog has both ahp-session:/ and copilotcli:/ entries for the same work. Start a new session in the main folder and let it run a long task that ends in a question to the user (ask_user/elicitation). Add or remove a folder in the workspace (for example a worktree) while that session is running. Watch agenthost.log for AgentHostCatalogReconciliation … superseded. Check whether the SDK session is destroyed and ~\.copilot\session-state\ is removed. I have not confirmed that step 4 is the only trigger, or what differs between the session that was destroyed and the three that survived. Related symptoms The same loss happened on Oct 16, when all active sessions vanished. The agenthost.log at 18:35 that day showed about 12 copilotcli:/… entries as sourceUnresolvable, meaning their state folders were already gone. Some copilotcli:/… entries (20186b6d, 3b59b702, 67b0178a, 82c7ab4d, 9f3a175e, ba09d539) are retried as sourceUnresolvable or superseded on every pass and never cleaned up. A session in assisted permission mode was destroyed while a tool call or elicitation was pending.
